findings.title: A double click on a reading search field at the app's panel size writes a reading the person never chose
findings.state_task_viewport: 373x410 DPR 1.5. key-configured (#picker-search), key-dense (#picker2/3/4-search), dial-configured and dial-groups (#pickerr-search, the rotation checklist), key-details (#pickerd-search). Task: open a reading list by clicking its search field, or close it with the panel's documented second click on the box (Escape never reaches the real panel). Real CDP press and release at the field's center, then a second press 120 ms later at the same point (clickCount 2). A triple click was also tried.
findings.observed: The first press scrolls the page by 100 to 333 px before the release: mousedown sets pointerOpening, the focus handler calls openList(true), and revealOpenList calls scrollBy. The second press therefore lands on a list row, and rows pick on mousedown. Candidate writes: second reading GPU Temperature to GPU Power, third reading to 'Write Rate', fourth reading to 'Total CPU Usage', and the rotation checklist ticks CPU CCD2 into rotationKeys or the collector group (a triple click ticks and then unticks: 2 frames). On d03 these four fields wrote nothing on a double click, because the page did not move under the pointer. The primary Reading picker (CPU (Tctl/Tdie) to CPU CCD1 (Tdie)) and the detail collector (second press on a move arrow reorders detailKeys) already wrote on d03, where row.scrollIntoView moved the page. So they are pre-existing, but R17 made the scroll deliberate and left them unguarded.
findings.evidence: MEASURED pd-dbl2-cand.json and pd-dbl2-base.json, pd-dbl3-cand.json and pd-dbl3-base.json, and pc-open.json (the element under the pointer at release is a list row in every case). READ pi-common.js revealOpenList, openList(pointerOpening), and the searchEl mousedown and focus handlers. The suite's R17 check (e2e-pi-panels.mjs:826) asserts scrollY > 0 and the field's position only. The pointer dismissal checks (331-361) run at 400x900, where nothing scrolls, so both pass on this behavior.
findings.affected_user: Everyone using a pointer: people who double-click a text field to select, and anyone closing a list with the documented second click on the box. The added rotation member or changed second, third or fourth reading can go unnoticed.
findings.correction: Never move the page while a press on the field is in progress. Run revealOpenList from the click (after release), not from the mousedown-driven focus. Also ignore row picks and checklist toggles from a press that begins within about 500 ms of a panel-initiated scroll, reusing the 450 ms armPress idiom. Apply the same guard to the primary picker and the detail collector.
findings.tradeoff: A deliberate pick within about 500 ms of opening is ignored once, and the reveal starts a few ms later.
findings.acceptance_test: At 373x410 DPR 1.5, a real double click and triple click at the center of #picker-search, #picker2-4-search, #pickerr-search and #pickerd-search on key-configured, key-dense, key-details, dial-configured and dial-groups writes 0 frames. A single click still reveals the list under the pinned header. The check lives in e2e-pi-panels at 373x410, and making revealOpenList run on mousedown again turns it red.

findings.title: Double clicking 'Pick another reading' replaces a missing reading with the first row of the list
findings.state_task_viewport: key-missing and dial-missing, 373x410 DPR 1.5. Task: repair a reading HWiNFO no longer lists, from the status region. Real double click on 'Pick another reading' at one point.
findings.observed: On the candidate, the first click runs reveal(), which scrolls so the Reading field sits under the pinned header, and the list opens on focus. The pointer (y 191 on the key, 207 on the dial) now rests on the first row, CPU (Tctl/Tdie). The second press picks it: readingKey f0099999:0:1000000 becomes f0000300:0:1000000 in 1 frame. On d03 the second press landed on the Reading section summary and nothing was written. A saved key that HWiNFO no longer lists cannot be picked again once it is replaced.
findings.evidence: MEASURED po-reveal-dbl-cand.json vs po-reveal-dbl-base.json (changed: [readingKey] on both panels, 0 writes on d03). READ pi-shell.js reveal(), picker branch (window.scrollBy to put the field under the header). The other reveal targets (setup steps, Data source, Change, Change gestures) wrote nothing on a double click.
findings.affected_user: Anyone repairing a missing reading with a pointer, and double-clickers in particular.
findings.correction: Use the same guard as AY01: after reveal() moves the page, ignore presses on list rows for about 500 ms. Alternatively, open the list on the next person's action instead of on the programmatic focus.
findings.tradeoff: A deliberate fast pick right after the reveal is ignored once.
findings.acceptance_test: On key-missing and dial-missing at 373x410, a double click on Pick another reading writes 0 frames, focus is in the Reading field, and the list is open. A later deliberate click on a row still picks it with 1 frame.

findings.title: Copy support report never announces its outcome: the new announcement calls an undefined 'hw'
findings.state_task_viewport: control-reset, key-configured and dial-configured, 373x410 DPR 1.5. Task: press Copy support report by keyboard with the plugin answering (clipboard rejects, execCommand fallback) and with the plugin silent for 3.6 s.
findings.observed: typeof hw is 'undefined' in the page. In pi-control.js, 'const speak = typeof hw !== "undefined" ? ... : () => {}' therefore resolves to the no-op, and the priming call never runs. A MutationObserver on every live region recorded nothing for 'Copied to clipboard' or 'Plugin not responding' on all three panels. Only the button's own text changes, for 2 s. Focus retention and aria-disabled do work.
findings.evidence: MEASURED pk-support-cand.json (typeofHw undefined, typeofHwShell object, said []). READ pi-control.js 21-25, pi-common.js 23 and pi-command.js 10 (hw is a local 'const hw = hwShell' inside each file's own closure). READ: the register's proof 'Persistence leg C' is e2e-pi-persistence.mjs 978-986, which tests the detail tile editor. No suite presses #support-report (only e2e-harness.mjs mentions it).
findings.affected_user: Screen reader users diagnosing a broken plugin, which is the case this button exists for.
findings.correction: In pi-control.js use the global: 'const shell = typeof hwShell !== "undefined" ? hwShell : null'. Prime with shell?.announce("support", "") and speak with shell?.announce("support", text, { repeat: true }). Add a panel check with a stubbed clipboard.
findings.tradeoff: None. It adds one polite announcement per press.
findings.acceptance_test: With the clipboard stubbed, Enter on Copy support report puts 'Copied to clipboard' (plugin answers) and 'Plugin not responding' (plugin silent 3 s) into the shell's polite region on the control, key and dial panels, with focus still on the button. The check fails if speak is a no-op.

findings.title: Several round 3 proofs pass on broken behavior or test something else
findings.register_ref: R12, R17, R10, R11, R20 (X02 carried over)
findings.state_task_viewport: The suites scripts/e2e-pi-panels.mjs and scripts/e2e-pi-persistence.mjs, read and not run, cross-checked against my lab runs at 373x410.
findings.observed: (1) The R17 check (line 826) asserts scroll and field position only. AY01 and AY02 pass it, and the pointer dismissal checks (331-361) run at 400x900, where nothing scrolls. (2) 'edit ...: one write' (line 137) still asserts sim.writes.length >= 1 (X02 item 1, carried over). (3) The preset seed sends 7 frames, and line 246 asserts >= 2. (4) R12 claims palette checks at 373 and 189, but the panel suite's palette checks (454-490) run at the default 400x900 (only the R17/R15 block sets 373x410), and the persistence suite sets no viewport. (5) R10's cited proof is the tile editor leg, so AY03 passes every suite. (6) The R11 check asserts the line's text, not the palette position. The R20 check covers only the same-problem path, so AY04 passes.

Assert the Gadget palette top at 373, and add a check where the problem changes before the answer to Check again.

findings.title: 'Check again' says 'no change yet' after a change, quotes an interval the plugin does not use, and Reload stays silent
findings.state_task_viewport: key-unavailable and key-stale, 373x410 DPR 1.5. Task: press Check again or Reload sensor list while HWiNFO has a problem.
findings.observed: (1) The source turns stale between the last render and the answer. The whole status is rebuilt (danger 'could not open a sensor feed' becomes warn 'No new Shared Memory measurements...'), and the new line says 'Checked again at 11:54:44 AM: no change yet.' (2) The source recovers, and the tree answer arrives 600 ms before the preview. 'no change yet' is shown and put into the polite region, then the status clears. (3) A stored pollIntervalMs of '100' reads 'every 100 ms' while the plugin clamps to 250 ms (src/poller.ts MIN_INTERVAL_MS 250; pi-model already has a 250 to 60000 clamp). (4) Reload sensor list with the source down gives no acknowledgement, because checkAskedAt is set only by the status button, although the shell comment says Reload is covered.
findings.evidence: MEASURED pb-ack.json steps 1b, 3, 4 and 6. READ pi-shell.js answerCheck, which fires on any tree after the ask and never compares with what was shown when the person pressed. READ pi-common.js picker refresh handler.
findings.affected_user: Anyone recovering from an outage, and screen reader users most (the contradiction is spoken).
findings.correction: Record the status signature when Check again is pressed, and write 'no change yet' only if the signature after the answer equals it. Take the interval from the model's clamped parser. Set checkAskedAt from Reload sensor list too, or drop Reload from the comment and the register.
findings.acceptance_test: Case (1): the problem changes during the press, and no 'no change yet' appears. A stored '100' reads '250 ms'. Reload while unavailable fills the line once. The same-problem path is unchanged.

findings.title: The Check again line makes assistive tech re-read the whole status region
findings.state_task_viewport: key-unavailable, 373x410. Task: press Check again with a screen reader.
findings.observed: The ack paragraph is filled inside #reading-status (role=status, aria-live=polite, no aria-atomic). The code comment says 'only that line's text changes, so only it is read out'.
findings.evidence: SB: in WAI-ARIA 1.2, role=status has an implicit aria-atomic value of true. MEASURED pq-atomic.json: Chromium's accessibility tree reports live: polite, atomic: true and relevant: additions text for #reading-status. Assistive tech that honors aria-atomic therefore reads the whole region (about 40 words plus the button names) each time the ack fills. How each screen reader handles this was INFERRED, not measured.
findings.correction: Speak the ack through the shell's separate announcer channel (hw.announce('status-ack', text, { repeat: true })) and keep the visible line out of the live region. Alternatively set aria-atomic="false" on #reading-status and check that a newly shown status is still read whole.
findings.tradeoff: aria-atomic=false changes how every status change is read (changed nodes only).
findings.acceptance_test: With NVDA and Chromium, or an accessibility event log, pressing Check again on key-unavailable speaks only the ack sentence.

findings.title: The healthy Gadget line is two lines, and its 'More' is plain text two folds away
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured and dial-configured with the sim's gadget data state (the free-HWiNFO route), 373x410 DPR 1.5.
findings.observed: The status is 48 px, two lines and 14 words, down from 96 px and 42 words on d03. The palette top is 172 on the key and 188 on the dial (116 and 132 when healthy; 221 and 237 on d03). The picker bottom is 336 and 352, which fits. 'More under Advanced, Connection.' is not a control. Its target #source-now sits inside two folded sections, while every other status pointer is a reveal button. The register asked for one line.
findings.evidence: MEASURED pn-gadget-cand.json and pn-gadget-base.json, pb-ack.json step 7. The first-pass acceptance C5 (palette top <= 150 on the key and <= 166 on the dial) fails by 22 px.
findings.affected_user: Every Gadget user, on every key and dial panel.
findings.correction: Either make 'More' a reveal button to #source-now (reveal opens both folds without remembering them), or drop the pointer sentence so the line fits on one line of about 24 px.
findings.tradeoff: A button adds a Tab stop. Dropping the sentence hides where the rest of the account lives.
findings.acceptance_test: With gadget data at 373x410, the status is <= 28 px, or 'More' is a button that puts focus on #source-now with 0 writes. The palette top is <= 150 on the key and <= 166 on the dial.

findings.title: Twin tags collide when both sensors carry the same HWiNFO instance mark
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-configured with a synthetic snapshot that adds 'CPU [#0]: Example 16-Core Processor: DTS', carrying the same label 'CPU (Tctl/Tdie)' as the '...: Enhanced' sensor. The rotation is [cpu, twin, gpu], 373x410.
findings.observed: Both chips show the pill '#0'. The difference (Enhanced vs DTS) appears only in the title and the sr-only 'from ...' text, so the visible disambiguation R07 promised fails.
findings.evidence: MEASURED pp-twins.json. READ twinTagOf: the /\[#(\d+)\]/ mark takes precedence over the tail after the last colon. INFERRED: HWiNFO lists several sensors for one CPU under the same '[#0]' mark (DTS and Enhanced blocks), so a same-label pair across them is plausible. The exact labels were not verified.
findings.affected_user: Power users with multi-block CPU sensors who rotate or detail same-named readings.
findings.correction: Use the mark only when the twins' marks differ. Otherwise use the tail after the last colon, or mark plus tail, truncated to 14 characters.
findings.tradeoff: Slightly longer pills in that case.
findings.acceptance_test: The synthetic snapshot shows two distinct pills ('Enhanced' and 'DTS'), and the drives still show '#0' and '#1'.

findings.title: The marked group jumps while the person works when the dial's reading starts outside every group
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups with readingKey set to GPU Power (in no group), 373x410. Task: pick a different dial reading, then tick readings into the marked group.
findings.observed: At load, group 1 is marked ('Readings for CPU') and nothing is settled, because no group holds the reading. After the person picks Hot Spot (held by group 2) in the dial's picker, the radio and label move to group 2 ('Readings for GPU') although the person never touched them. The register says the group is settled once per page, never while the person works.
findings.evidence: MEASURED pe-names.json step 4. READ renderRotationSet: collectorSettled becomes true only when a holding group is found.
findings.correction: Set collectorSettled = true after the first render with groups, whether or not a holding group was found.
findings.acceptance_test: The same sequence leaves group 1 marked, and the e2e R36 check (reading held by group 2 at load) still passes.

findings.title: An armed remove disarms silently on any rebuild and leaves 'Press again' as the last spoken words
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups, 373x410. Task: arm group 1's remove, then a plugin settings echo arrives (the dial is turned) or a sensorTree message arrives, then press again.
findings.observed: After the echo the button shows 'x' again, focus stays on it, and the polite region still holds 'Press again to remove group 1 and its 2 readings.' The next press only arms again (0 writes), so a screen reader user hears 'Press again' twice and nothing is removed. A sensorTree message does the same. Related: after typing a group name and clicking straight into another group's name field, group 1's listbox keeps its old accessible name ('Group 1, CPU'), because rebuilds are skipped while a name field has focus.
findings.evidence: MEASURED pa-arm.json (the last two rows) and pe-names.json step 3. READ armPress (the arm lives on the DOM node) and the renderRotationSet focus guard.
findings.affected_user: Screen reader and keyboard users. It happens only when an echo or tree arrives while armed, which is rare.
findings.correction: When a rebuild replaces an armed button, carry the arm over if the group's member keys are unchanged. Otherwise say 'Not removed.', as Replace says 'Not replaced. Nothing was changed.' Rebuild the list labels when a name field blurs, even without a change.
findings.tradeoff: Carrying an arm across a rebuild must compare member keys, or it could confirm against a changed group.
findings.acceptance_test: Arm, push an echo, press again: either the unchanged group is removed in 1 frame, or the region says it was not removed before re-arming.

findings.title: Picking Custom from Elite sends seven frames, the first with no gestures
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups and dial-custom-gestures, 373x410. Task: pick Custom from Elite by keyboard.
findings.observed: The first frame carries only controlPreset custom. For that instant the runtime runs Custom with Legacy fallbacks, so there is no group switch. Then 6 identical frames follow, each carrying all six seeded gestures (5 when a gesture was already set). The suite asserts >= 2.
findings.evidence: MEASURED pf-integrity.json (changed-key counts per frame [1,7,7,7,7,7,7]) and pi-r01-cand.json. On d03 the seed also sent 6 frames, but carrying Elite.
findings.affected_user: Nobody visibly. It is wasteful traffic and a torn state for an instant.
findings.correction: Stage the six gesture fields with the non-saving useSettings pattern (as groupsStage does) and let one save carry the preset and the seed together.
findings.tradeoff: The seed and preset must still land after the shell's own save (keep the R01 ordering).
findings.acceptance_test: Elite to Custom by keyboard produces exactly 1 frame carrying controlPreset custom and the six seeded gestures, and the R01 checks still pass.

keep: Zero writes on observation holds on the candidate across 18 fixtures with real pointer and keys, including the new surfaces. The battery covered chip hover, Change, Check again, setup, source, Pick, Reload, every summary twice, Open all, arming and leaving every group remove and Merge, arming and leaving Replace, 90 Tab and 90 Shift+Tab, listbox arrows and Alt+Home at the first place, focus and blur of every text field, pointer leave and window blur.
